claim_text: Robert Goddard launches the world's first liquid-fueled rocket at Auburn, Massachusetts.
source: Standard histories of rocketry; NASA and Smithsonian historical records
notes: Foundational to spaceflight; 2.5-second flight, ~12.5 m altitude.

claim_text: NBC launches as the first permanent national radio broadcasting network in the US.
source: Standard broadcasting histories
notes: RCA-owned; established the national-network model for mass media.

claim_text: Charles Lindbergh completes the first solo nonstop transatlantic flight (New York–Paris) in the Spirit of St. Louis.
source: Smithsonian NASM records; standard aviation histories
notes: Catalyzed public and commercial confidence in aviation.

claim_text: Philo Farnsworth demonstrates the first working all-electronic television image transmission.
source: Standard histories of television technology
notes: First electronic TV image, San Francisco lab, 7 Sep 1927.

claim_text: The Jazz Singer premieres as the first feature-length film with synchronized recorded dialogue, launching the sound-film era.
source: Standard film histories; Vitaphone records
notes: Ended the silent-film era; Warner Bros./Vitaphone system.

claim_text: Clyde Tombaugh discovers Pluto at Lowell Observatory, the first trans-Neptunian object found.
source: Lowell Observatory records; standard astronomy references
notes: Reclassified as dwarf planet in 2006; unaffected as a discovery milestone.

claim_text: The Empire State Building is completed in New York City, then the tallest building in the world (381 m).
source: Standard architectural/engineering references
notes: Held world's-tallest title until 1970; built in ~13 months.

claim_text: Ernest Lawrence builds the first working cyclotron at Berkeley, enabling particle acceleration.
source: Standard physics histories; Nobel records (Lawrence, 1939)
notes: First ~11 cm proof-of-concept 1930-31; larger machines followed 1932.

claim_text: The Tennessee Valley Authority is established, a federal authority for regional electrification and river development.
source: US federal statute record; standard New Deal histories
notes: New Deal; both infrastructure and institution — classified by its landmark-institution significance.

claim_text: The Glass–Steagall Banking Act creates federal deposit insurance (FDIC) and separates commercial and investment banking.
source: US federal statute record; standard economic histories
notes: Reshaped US financial regulation for decades; FDIC still operates.

claim_text: The Social Security Act establishes national old-age pensions and unemployment insurance.
source: US federal statute record; Social Security Administration histories
notes: Founding of the modern US social-insurance system.

claim_text: Hoover Dam on the Colorado River is completed, then the world's largest concrete structure and hydroelectric dam.
source: US Bureau of Reclamation records
notes: Construction 1931–1936; dedicated Sep 1935; anchored to 1935 dedication.

claim_text: Wallace Carothers's team at DuPont first synthesizes nylon, the first fully synthetic polymer fiber.
source: Standard histories of materials science; DuPont records
notes: First synthesized 1935; commercial 1938-39; founded the synthetic-fiber industry.

claim_text: The Douglas DC-3 makes its first flight, becoming the airliner that made passenger air travel commercially viable.
source: Smithsonian NASM records; standard aviation histories
notes: First flight Dec 1935; entered service 1936.

claim_text: The Northern Expedition ends with nominal national reunification under the Nationalist (KMT) government seated at Nanjing.
source: Standard histories of Republican China
notes: Campaign 1926–1928; anchored to 1928 completion; began the 'Nanjing decade' of partial modernization.

claim_text: Academia Sinica (中央研究院), China's national academy of sciences, is founded at Nanjing.
source: Academia Sinica historical records; standard references
notes: First national modern research-academy institution; both science and durable institution.

claim_text: The Central Bank of China is established in Shanghai as the Nationalist government's central bank.
source: Standard economic histories of Republican China
notes: Part of Nanjing-decade financial-institution building.

claim_text: Pei Wenzhong discovers the first Peking Man (Homo erectus) skullcap at Zhoukoudian.
source: Standard paleoanthropology references
notes: Major hominin find on Chinese soil by a Chinese scientist; specimens later lost in WWII.

claim_text: The Mass Education Movement's rural-reconstruction experiment at Ding County (Dingxian) scales mass literacy and rural development, led by Y.C. James Yen.
source: Standard histories of Republican-era rural reconstruction
notes: Diffuse program ~1926–1937; anchored ~1929; a landmark in modern Chinese mass-education.

claim_text: The Nanjing-decade government undertakes a national railway, highway, and telecommunications expansion program.
source: Standard economic histories of Republican China
notes: Diffuse buildout ~1928–1937; anchored mid-decade; interrupted by war from 1937. Category populated but low-precision.

claim_text: The fabi (法币) currency reform abandons the silver standard and unifies a managed national paper currency.
source: Standard economic histories of Republican China
notes: Nov 1935; a major monetary-regime shift, though later undermined by wartime inflation.

claim_text: The Chinese Communist Party's Red Army completes the Long March, consolidating Mao Zedong's leadership and the CCP's survival.
source: Standard histories of the Chinese Communist Party
notes: Oct 1934–Oct 1935; primarily a military retreat, admitted for its durable political-institutional consequence, not as a battlefield outcome.

claim_text: Chinese-owned cotton-textile firms (e.g., the Rong family's Shenxin mills) become the leading modern manufacturing sector in the lower Yangtze.
source: Standard economic histories of Republican China
notes: Diffuse; anchored ~1930. Included to populate the industrial category honestly, with low precision noted.
